public_rationale: The contract reads 'commodity' as meaning that rival models are easy to swap, that buyers choose mainly on price, and that prices for a given capability fall quickly under competition. Evidence of buyers choosing on performance, paying for frontier models and staying with one provider would contradict it. Part of the claim holds. Epoch AI (March 12, 2025) found that the price of reaching a given benchmark result fell 9x to 900x per year (e1). Menlo Ventures' mid-2025 report says switching vendors is relatively easy (e3). Part does not hold. The same report says builders 'consistently choose frontier models over cheaper, faster alternatives' and 'pay for performance' (e2). It also reports that 66% of builders upgraded within their existing provider, 23% did not switch models, and only 11% switched vendors (e3). These buyer findings match the contract's contradiction condition. The price findings match part of the support condition. The evidence does not show whether prices were pushed toward cost.
limitations: The buyer evidence comes from a single survey of builders by a venture firm, from mid-2025, months before the December 2025 post.
Epoch measured price declines at benchmark milestones. It did not measure whether buyers treat models as interchangeable, and it found no clear evidence that falling margins explain the declines.
There are no profit-margin data showing whether prices reached cost.
'Commodity' is partly a rhetorical label, so the result depends on the reading used.

statement.excerpt: Coke and Pepsi are commodities; genAI models are, too.
statement.document_title: The core misconception that is driving American AI policy

our_interpretation: Plain reading: generative AI models from rival providers are broadly interchangeable, so buyers choose mainly on price, and prices are pushed toward cost.
Present-tense claim: it describes the market in 2025 up to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that models are easily swapped, that buyers choose mainly on price, and that prices for a given capability fall quickly under competition.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that buyers choose mainly on performance, pay for frontier models over cheaper equivalents, and stick with particular providers, so models are differentiated rather than interchangeable.

evidence.explanation: The price of any given capability level falls very fast. That is consistent with commodity-like competition once a capability is matched.
